title: Patch, Don't Rewrite: Post-Drift Rule Updates for LogRules-Style LLM Log Parsers

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to define and motivate the problem of updating an LLM log parser's rule repository when log templates drift. Papers [1], [5], [20], and [28] discuss concept drift adaptation, which is closely related to handling changes in data distributions over time. However, none of these papers specifically address the problem of updating rule repositories for log parsers under template drift. Papers [2], [3], [6], [7], [8], [9], [10], [15], and [14] focus on log parsing but do not define or motivate the specific problem of rule repository updates under template drift. Therefore, no prior paper establishes the same purpose.

### Mechanism
The contribution introduces the rule repository update problem for LogRules-style parsers and empirically contrasts full rewriting against conservative patching. Papers [11], [12], [13], [17], [18], and [19] discuss various forms of rewriting or patching, including incremental updates to rules, binary rewriting, and patch graph rewriting. Paper [11] specifically addresses incremental updating techniques for rule maintenance, which is substantively equivalent to the mechanism described here. Although the application domains differ (association rules vs. log parsing), the underlying primitive of incremental rule updates is the same.

### Evaluation
The evaluation compares Naive Rewrite and Patch approaches, showing that Patch achieves +8.1 FGA points over Naive Rewrite. Papers [14] and [15] introduce benchmarks and metrics for log parsing, including template precision and accuracy, which are substantively equivalent evaluation designs. Paper [14] focuses on character-level template precision, while paper [15] evaluates parsing accuracy. Both use standard log parsing metrics and validation setups, making the evaluation design covered.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of LLM-based log parsing under template drift. Papers [2], [3], [6], [7], [8], [9], [10], [14], and [15] all address log parsing using LLMs or other methods, making the domain covered. While the specific focus on template drift is narrower, it falls within the broader application area of log parsing.
